You are an adversarial reviewer for the shopsystem-product lead shop. Your job: try to prove that the migration plan CANNOT be executed as written, and produce the complete list of required conditions to proceed. Be ruthless — a finding you soften is a finding the authority hits later.

MATERIAL (read all of it):
- The plan under review: /workspace/drafts/migration-plan.md (rev 2, 393 lines)
- The new basis (branch experiment/new-basis, checked out at /home/vscode/basis-experiment/basis/): README.md, principles.md, glossary.md, artifacts/ (12 typedefs), processes/ (7 process definitions — especially definition-chain-migration.md), types/, fitness/, guidelines/, roles/, skills/, tools/
- The compiled principle rendering: /workspace/.claude/shop/principles.md (nine principles)
- The corpus the plan migrates lives on /workspace main: adr/, pdr/ (or adrs/pdrs — check), briefs, intents, candidates, sessions, findings/, features/, docs, drafts/

THE PRODUCT AUTHORITY (David) HAS SEEDED FOUR FINDINGS — verify each against the material, sharpen it with evidence (file:line), and extend it; do not merely confirm:
1. Vocabulary: the plan uses "kind" (lines 72, 181, 215, 228, 233, 245, 307) where basis/glossary.md line 21-22 rules the term is "artifact type — … Not 'kind'". Sweep for other undefined or wrongly-used terms in the plan against the glossary.
2. F-codes: the plan calls them "rewrite families — clusters of decision records that collapse into one rewritten record each (F2 fleet … F15 licensing)" and never explains further. Adversarial questions: (a) Is the full F2–F15 list defined ANYWHERE? (b) Collapsing many ADRs into one record per family — does that overload what a decision record can carry, and is that collapse being decided BEFORE the decision-record chain (typedef/guideline/fitness) exists to define what one record may hold? Which principle does deciding-before-defining violate? (c) Where exactly does the authority give review input on EACH artifact being migrated — trace the review touchpoints through definition-chain-migration.md (authority-review, approve-chain, "spot-checks per the attention architecture" — is that attention architecture defined anywhere?) and state precisely what the authority sees and rules on, per artifact vs per chain vs per family.
3. Opaque references: the plan (and its presentation surface) leans on raw work-item ids (lead-jozud.2 line ~72) and record ids with no in-document explanation. Sweep for every reference a reader cannot resolve from the document itself.
4. Readiness — THE BIG ONE: David's claim: "we don't have the definitions of the artifacts being migrated, so it would not be possible to rewrite anything. The current artifacts are all meta-artifacts needed to create those definitions, processes and skills." Verify: which artifact types does the run order name (principle-set, decision records adr/pdr, framework spec, PM records intent/candidate/brief/session, findings, scenarios) and which of those have ANY chain link existing today in basis/? (basis/artifacts/ has typedefs for the meta-layer: artifact-typedef, process-definition, principle-set, decision-brief, review-record, etc. — check which run-order types map to an existing typedef and which have nothing.) The definition-chain-migration process builds the chain INSIDE each run (build-chain step) — does the plan SAY that anywhere? Does the plan state per-run entry conditions (keepers list exists, chain inputs available, tooling present)? 

ADDITIONALLY, run your own adversarial sweep:
5. Tooling preconditions: definition-chain-migration.md references tools/compile_process.py, tools/lint_basis.py --derive-chain, and an `archive-move` command it says "the migration plan's review must approve" and "until it exists the step blocks". Check what exists in basis/tools/ and on main. Does the plan surface the archive-move approval as part of its asks? Any other blocked step or missing tool?
6. Principle screen: check the PLAN itself against each of the nine principles (define-good-up-front, governed-context, no-orphan-activities — does the overall migration declare its exit/round caps?, use-defined-terms, external-standards-first, single-source-of-truth — census duplicated anywhere?, feedback-loops-with-consumers, delivery-verified — what demonstrates a run/the migration done in the running system?, least-context). One verdict per principle with evidence.
7. Internal consistency: do the summary-table numbers add up against the lane tables? Does every authority-call row in the tables map to an Ask-2 item and vice versa? Do run-order types cover every keep-rewrite row's type?
8. The plan claims "cold-read verified" — yet the real reader (the authority) could not answer the F-code and review-input questions from it. Treat the prior cold-read check as itself defective and say why it passed wrongly if you can tell.

DELIVERABLE (your final text, raw structured markdown, no preamble):
A) Findings list: id, severity (blocker/major/minor), one-line claim, evidence (file:line), consequence.
B) REQUIRED CONDITIONS TO PROCEED: a numbered list of every condition that must hold before run 1 can start, each tagged one of: SATISFIED (evidence), LEAD-WORK (the lead shop can build/fix it — say what), AUTHORITY-RULING (only the authority can settle it — say the question).
C) One paragraph: is David's readiness objection structurally correct, partially correct, or a pure communication gap — with the precise mechanism.

Reach for it when a shape rests on an assumption cheap enough to test in hours or days and honest enough to kill the bet if it fails.
- pol-probe-advisor: Select the right Proof-of-Life probe flavor for a given hypothesis by working backward from the harshest truth, not from tooling comfort. Reach for it inside shaping when you know an assumption needs testing but aren't sure whether it's a feasibility check, a task test, a narrative, a simulation, or a vibe-coded probe.
- press-release: Amazon-style "working backwards" PR/FAQ framing — draft the customer-facing announcement before building, as a forcing function for clarity and customer-centricity. Reach for it inside a product-narrative session to test whether a direction is genuinely compelling from the outside.
- prioritization: Order the candidates and commitments into a defensible sequence, capturing the ordering and its rationale as a prioritization record
- prioritization-advisor: Select the prioritization method that fits the current context — MoSCoW, RICE, ICE, weighted scoring, Kano, Value/Effort, Cost of Delay — instead of defaulting to one dogmatically. Reach for it inside a prioritization session before scoring anything, to pick the right lens for the stage, data, and decision at hand.

- problem-statement: Turn a request or a raw job into a crisp, user-centered problem statement using the "I am / trying to / but / because / which makes me feel" frame, so intent names a person and a barrier, not a solution. Use inside the discovery-dialogue to fix the problem before any solutioning.
- product-narrative: Render the product's current state outward as an honest, grounded narrative, producing a README, site, or current-state revision that traces to real capability
- recommendation-canvas: Structured evaluation of a candidate option — outcomes, hypotheses, assumptions, risks, value, metrics — treating each option as a bet to validate, not a commitment. - reconcile-and-close: Reconcile a completed BC dispatch by consuming its work_done outbox row and closing the corresponding bead as one atomic reconcile-and-close action via the reconcile-and-close executable wrapper

Use when decomposing an Epic into scenarios, when a scenario carries multiple When/Then, or when an assigned unit is too big to build and review cleanly.

# Migration plan: rebaseline against the approved basis

Census run 2026-08-22 by four independent lanes over the live tree,
verifying the 2026-08-04 census where it overlapped and judging
everything after it fresh. This plan is the rebaseline's action table
plus the run order for `definition-chain-migration`; approving it starts
Phase 1.

## How to rule

**Vocabulary for this document.** A *chain* is a type's full definition
of good (typedef, guideline, fitness set, process, roles, compiled
skill); one `definition-chain-migration` run builds a chain and rewrites
that type's keepers through it. Actions: *keep-rewrite* — content still
binding, re-authored through the chain; *keep* — stays as-is, no rewrite
(scenarios and operational files); *retire* — value passed, moves to an
archive branch (never `main`); *terminal* — junk or never-advanced,
deleted or closed as never-accepted. The *F-codes* in reason cells are
the census's rewrite families — clusters of decision records that
collapse into one rewritten record each (F2 fleet … F15 licensing). The
*trust break* is the 2026-08-03 quality failure that triggered the
re-founding (intent-013).

**Ask 1 (block): approve the action table and run order.** Every row
carries its lane's one-line evidence. **Ask 2 (three rulings): the
authority calls below** — each has a recommendation and a default.
Silence on a call is itself handled: the default carries it into the
decision-chain run's review as an open item; nothing is retired or
deleted by silence.

2	type: glossary
3	id: glossary
4	owner: product-authority
5	status: approved

8	updated: 2026-08-20
9	---
10	
11	# Glossary
12	
13	## How the list combines
14	
15	The defined-term list is this glossary combined with every schema element
16	name. Per the `use-defined-terms` principle, a writer choosing between
17	terms uses one of these when one fits.
18	
19	## Terms
20	
21	- **artifact type** — a named, schema-defined document type (e.g.
22	  `decision-brief`); the term the schema registry uses. Not "kind".
23	- **data type** — a named, schema-defined structure that is not a
24	  human-readable document (e.g. `review`); passed between process steps.
25	- **simple type** — a JSON Schema primitive (`string`, `integer`,
26	  `boolean`, `array`, `object`), usable inline without registration.
27	- **typedef** — the single source a type is generated from; templates and
28	  schema fragments are its renderings (owned by shopsystem-knowledge).
29	- **schema** — the machine-checkable shape of a type: fields, types,
30	  enums, required sections.
31	- **process definition** — the source of truth for a process: header
32	  (purpose, outcomes, roles), data section, steps section.
33	- **step** — one unit of a process: an agent step (carries a prompt) or a
34	  runtime step (carries `set`, `run`, or `branches`; no prose).
35	- **rendering** — a generated output of a definition (a skill, a
36	  diagram, a template); never edited by hand, never the source of truth.
37	- **guiding statement** — an optional header element of a process
38	  definition that directs judgment across the whole process; compiled
39	  into every rendering.
40	- **fitness set** — judged (never executed) Given/When/Then scenarios
41	  scoring an artifact type's quality.
42	- **guideline** — prose quality rules for an artifact type, each with a
43	  test, a criterion, and a yes/no decision.
44	- **role** — a named seat with a capability contract and
45	  accountabilities; sequencing lives in process definitions, not roles.
46	- **principle** — a standing rule about how we work: name, statement,
47	  rationale, implications (see the principles document's opening
48	  definition).
49	- **seed layer** — the hand-approved definitions the regress terminates
50	  at: the principle set plus one typedef per definition document type.
51	- **owner** — the seat that approves changes to a definition; named in
52	  every definition's frontmatter.
53	- **definition chain** — the six linked definitions of good for one
54	  artifact type; required before instances are authored or rewritten.
55	- **keeper** — a corpus record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
56	  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
57	- **rewrite-forward** — the default for keepers: re-author to the
58	  approved standard; repair-in-place only for records already at the bar.
59	- **rebaseline** — Phase 1 of the re-founding arc: the active tree comes
60	  to hold only chain-conforming records; retired mass moves to the
61	  archive.
62	- **scope** (of a principle set) — the level the set governs and whose
63	  context it loads into: working (every activity) or architecture (the
64	  designed system).
65	- **transcript** — the runtime log of turns; unscoped, not a governed
66	  artifact, never loaded into context.
67	- **conversation** — a scoped, bounded discussion attached to exactly one
68	  anchor; every conversation belongs to a process.
69	- **conversation type** — discovery (anchor: a session record), review
70	  (anchor: a review record and its rulings), or work (anchor: a work
71	  item).
72	- **session record** — the anchor record of a discovery conversation:
73	  outcome, produced and revised lists, open threads, select quotes.

# Glossary

## How the list combines

The defined-term list is this glossary combined with every schema element
name. Per the `use-defined-terms` principle, a writer choosing between
terms uses one of these when one fits.

## Terms

- **artifact type** — a named, schema-defined document type (e.g.
  `decision-brief`); the term the schema registry uses. Not "kind".
- **data type** — a named, schema-defined structure that is not a
  human-readable document (e.g. `review`); passed between process steps.
- **simple type** — a JSON Schema primitive (`string`, `integer`,
  `boolean`, `array`, `object`), usable inline without registration.
- **typedef** — the single source a type is generated from; templates and
  schema fragments are its renderings (owned by shopsystem-knowledge).
- **schema** — the machine-checkable shape of a type: fields, types,
  enums, required sections.
- **process definition** — the source of truth for a process: header
  (purpose, outcomes, roles), data section, steps section.
- **step** — one unit of a process: an agent step (carries a prompt) or a
  runtime step (carries `set`, `run`, or `branches`; no prose).
- **rendering** — a generated output of a definition (a skill, a
  diagram, a template); never edited by hand, never the source of truth.
- **guiding statement** — an optional header element of a process
  definition that directs judgment across the whole process; compiled
  into every rendering.
- **fitness set** — judged (never executed) Given/When/Then scenarios
  scoring an artifact type's quality.
- **guideline** — prose quality rules for an artifact type, each with a
  test, a criterion, and a yes/no decision.
- **role** — a named seat with a capability contract and
  accountabilities; sequencing lives in process definitions, not roles.
- **principle** — a standing rule about how we work: name, statement,
  rationale, implications (see the principles document's opening
  definition).
- **seed layer** — the hand-approved definitions the regress terminates
  at: the principle set plus one typedef per definition document type.
- **owner** — the seat that approves changes to a definition; named in
  every definition's frontmatter.
- **definition chain** — the six linked definitions of good for one
  artifact type; required before instances are authored or rewritten.
- **keeper** — a corpus record whose action is keep-rewrite; rewritten
  forward through its type's approved chain, never used as-is.
- **rewrite-forward** — the default for keepers: re-author to the
  approved standard; repair-in-place only for records already at the bar.
- **rebaseline** — Phase 1 of the re-founding arc: the active tree comes
  to hold only chain-conforming records; retired mass moves to the
  archive.
- **scope** (of a principle set) — the level the set governs and whose
  context it loads into: working (every activity) or architecture (the
  designed system).
- **transcript** — the runtime log of turns; unscoped, not a governed
  artifact, never loaded into context.
- **conversation** — a scoped, bounded discussion attached to exactly one
  anchor; every conversation belongs to a process.
- **conversation type** — discovery (anchor: a session record), review
  (anchor: a review record and its rulings), or work (anchor: a work
  item).
- **session record** — the anchor record of a discovery conversation:
  outcome, produced and revised lists, open threads, select quotes.
- **review** — one bounded conversation in which the authority rules on
  presented material. Replaces "sitting".
- **review record** — the anchor record of a review: the material
  presented and the rulings issued.
- **ruling** — a decision the authority records during a review; numbered
  (Rn) in the experiment index and binding on the corpus it governs.
- **park** — the failsafe for work that cannot pass review within its
  round cap: set aside with a filed finding.
- **round cap** — the declared maximum review rounds before a loop's
  failsafe exit fires.
- **action** — the approved choice for one record: keep-rewrite, retire,
  or terminal, with its target.
- **action table** — the table of records and their actions; approved row
  by row or in blocks at a review. Drives any bulk record change.
- **migration plan** — the rebaseline's action table plus the order of
  the per-type migration runs. Replaces "rebaseline bill".
- **experiment index** — the new-basis experiment's README: the
  walkthrough, the numbered rulings, and the review state.
- **run** — one execution of a process, anchored to a work item; states:
  running, held, done, cancelled.
- **hold** — a run state: paused with its step and data preserved in its
  anchor; a held run is resumed or cancelled, never dropped.
- **checkpoint** — updating a conversation's anchor when a transcript
  ends mid-conversation; a checkpoint is not a close.
- **branched conversation** — a conversation run as a sub-process of
  another run; its anchor records the parent (`branched-from`).

# Cold reviewer

You simulate the product authority reading cold: technically expert,
~5 minutes of attention, no knowledge of the annex or the author's context.
You treat an unintroduced term or an ask you cannot decide as a defect.

**Accountable for:**
- Reading the presentation exactly once, top to bottom, alone — nothing else.
- Reporting stumbles in reading order, with quotes.
- Listing every term that arrives before the document explains it.
- A per-ask decidability verdict: confident / wobbly / cannot decide, with
  what is missing.
- An overload verdict: right-sized for one reading, or what to defer.
- Honesty: report only real reading problems, never invented findings that
  make the review look thorough; report a clean section as clean.

**Domain (exclusive):** the round's verdict. The author revises; the
reviewer alone decides what this round found.

**Competencies:** software-architecture literacy (reads standards citations
without glosses); stakeholder empathy (limited-attention reading); the
fitness set at `../fitness/decision-brief.fitness.md`, which this role
judges.

# Artifact type: decision-brief

## Identity and ancestry

- **Type:** `decision-brief`
- **Generic type:** request — it requests decisions.
  **Ancestry:** `request → decision-brief` (generic fallback: any validator
  that knows `request` may check this type at that level).
- **User-need quadrant:** action + work — the reader
  is deciding, now. One quadrant per document; a brief that drifts into
  explanation fails its type.
- **Produced by:** [`../processes/stakeholder-presentation.md`](../processes/stakeholder-presentation.md).
  **Consumed by:** the product authority, at a review.

## Required frontmatter

`type`, `status` (draft | delivered | decided), `date`, `reader`,
`decisions-requested` (count), `annex` (link), `verified-by` (cold-read
round record). Schema-validated; unknown keys rejected (closed field set,
per the authority's strictness directive).

## Required sections

1. **The answer first** — SCQA opening, ≤4 sentences, then the
   recommendation; states which asks gate work and which default on silence.
2. **Asks** — each: question → recommendation → inline evidence → default.
   Block-approval asks state what approval binds vs what stays a
   drafting default.
3. **Deferred** (if anything is) — deferrals are notes, never asks.
4. **Annex link** — the full material, labeled optional.

## Commitment (Definition of Done)

A decision-brief is done when: the reader can make every requested decision
from the brief alone in one short reading; budgets hold (decision layer
≤ ~400 words, total ≤ ~1,500); an independent cold read has passed it (O3 of
the producing process). **Consequence on failure:** the brief returns to the
author for re-forming — it is not deliverable, and decisions made from a
failed brief are not recorded as approvals.

## Sources

ISO/IEC/IEEE 15289 (generic content types); DITA-style ancestry
declaration; Scrum's artifact-commitment pairing; layer and ask structure
from Minto/SCQA, BLUF, and government briefing-note practice.

## Derived review checklist (from this schema — cite-or-delete rule)

- Frontmatter validates; unknown keys rejected. *(schema)*
- Answer-first section states gate-vs-default. *(§Required sections 1)*

You simulate the product authority reading cold: technically expert,
~5 minutes of attention, no knowledge of the annex or the author's context.
You treat an unintroduced term or an ask you cannot decide as a defect.

**Accountable for:**
- Reading the presentation exactly once, top to bottom, alone — nothing else.
- Reporting stumbles in reading order, with quotes.

# Artifact type: decision-brief

## Identity and ancestry

- **Type:** `decision-brief`
- **Generic type:** request — it requests decisions.
  **Ancestry:** `request → decision-brief` (generic fallback: any validator
  that knows `request` may check this type at that level).
- **User-need quadrant:** action + work — the reader
  is deciding, now. One quadrant per document; a brief that drifts into
  explanation fails its type.
- **Produced by:** [`../processes/stakeholder-presentation.md`](../processes/stakeholder-presentation.md).
  **Consumed by:** the product authority, at a review.

## Required frontmatter

`type`, `status` (draft | delivered | decided), `date`, `reader`,
`decisions-requested` (count), `annex` (link), `verified-by` (cold-read
round record). Schema-validated; unknown keys rejected (closed field set,
per the authority's strictness directive).

## Required sections

1. **The answer first** — SCQA opening, ≤4 sentences, then the
   recommendation; states which asks gate work and which default on silence.
2. **Asks** — each: question → recommendation → inline evidence → default.
   Block-approval asks state what approval binds vs what stays a
   drafting default.
3. **Deferred** (if anything is) — deferrals are notes, never asks.
4. **Annex link** — the full material, labeled optional.

## Commitment (Definition of Done)

A decision-brief is done when: the reader can make every requested decision
from the brief alone in one short reading; budgets hold (decision layer
≤ ~400 words, total ≤ ~1,500); an independent cold read has passed it (O3 of
the producing process). **Consequence on failure:** the brief returns to the
author for re-forming — it is not deliverable, and decisions made from a
failed brief are not recorded as approvals.

## Sources

ISO/IEC/IEEE 15289 (generic content types); DITA-style ancestry
declaration; Scrum's artifact-commitment pairing; layer and ask structure
from Minto/SCQA, BLUF, and government briefing-note practice.

# Adversarial review — migration-plan.md rev 2

## A) Findings

Severity legend: **BLOCKER** = the plan cannot be executed (or lawfully approved) as written; **MAJOR** = execution would produce ungoverned or unverifiable results; **MINOR** = defect, containable.

**F1 — BLOCKER — The archive tool the process requires does not exist and the plan never asks for it.**
Evidence: `/home/vscode/basis-experiment/basis/processes/definition-chain-migration.md:104-107` — "The `archive-move` command in `archive-retired` is the archive contract tool **the migration plan's review must approve** … Until it exists the step blocks." `archive-move` is not in `/workspace/bin/` (contains only agent-vault-check, agent-vault-provision, check-knowledge-artifacts, doctor, gen-scenario-refs, ops-coordinates, shop-shell), not on PATH, and the string "archive-move" appears nowhere in `/workspace/drafts/migration-plan.md`. Ask 1 and Ask 2 (lines 35-41, 88-105) contain no approval of the archive contract.
Consequence: every run dead-ends at `archive-retired`; O3 unreachable; and the one review that is contractually supposed to approve the tool passes without approving it.

**F2 — BLOCKER — The approved process definition has a broken control flow: `derive-chain` has no `next`, so `exemplar-rewrite` is unreachable.**
Evidence: `definition-chain-migration.md:132-140` — the `derive-chain` step ends at `run:` with no `next:`; every other non-terminal step has one. The compiled mermaid (lines 64-77) faithfully shows it: `build_chain --> derive_chain` then nothing; `exemplar_rewrite --> authority_review` has no inbound edge. The compiler reproduced the bug; the "compiles and screens" check (line 267) passed a process whose flow cannot reach its own review loop.
Consequence: run 1 halts after chain derivation; no exemplar, no authority review, no approval — structurally, per the definition, nothing can be rewritten. This is the strongest literal form of David's objection.

**F3 — BLOCKER — The plan's retire/terminal mass has no process that moves it.**
Evidence: plan lines 85-86 "Junk trees (`terminal`) delete at execution start; retire mass moves to archive branches at each run's `archive-retired` step" vs. `definition-chain-migration.md:242-247` — `archive-retired` takes input `demoted` only, and `demoted` is produced solely by `rewrite-keepers` (keepers that failed rewrite). The 163 pre-decided retires and 14 terminals are never in `keepers`, never in `demoted`, and no other process exists in `basis/processes/` for deletion, closure ("closed as never-accepted", plan line 28-29), or scenario-file retirement (run 6, lines 82-84, is explicitly "no chain needed" — i.e., not a `definition-chain-migration` run at all, under a heading that says "one `definition-chain-migration` run per type", line 65).
Consequence: the bulk of the plan's effect (177 of 318 records) is an orphan activity — `no-orphan-activities` violation; executed, it would be an ungoverned mass mutation; unexecuted, the plan's stated outcome never occurs.

**F4 — BLOCKER — The F-code rewrite families are defined only in a document this plan retires, and no process input can carry them.**
Evidence: plan line 29-31 names only "F2 fleet … F15 licensing"; the full family map (membership, target record counts, F1 folding, F11 empty) exists solely at `/workspace/drafts/rebaseline-bill.md:55-69` — which the plan supersedes (frontmatter line 5) and retires (Appendix A, line 358: "rebaseline-bill (superseded by this plan)"). Meanwhile the process signature is `parameters: [artifact_type, keepers]` (`definition-chain-migration.md:111`) with `keepers: string[]` — there is no data slot through which the collapse map, or any reason-cell directive ("folds into F2", line 111; "sc06-deferral clause scrubbed at rewrite", line 132; "recover falsified date", line 165; "collapses with adr-066", line 168; "may fold into F9", line 156; "re-verify deferred primitive first", line 117), can lawfully enter `rewrite-keepers`.
Consequence: run 2 must either load a retired, ungoverned document into the generating context (`governed-context` violation) or silently drop the operative rewrite instructions the authority approved. Both are failure. Also directly: (a) the F2–F15 list is defined nowhere the plan governs; (b) answered below in F5/F6.

**F5 — BLOCKER — Collapse decisions are made before the definition that would license them exists (decide-before-define).**
Evidence: the plan fixes many→one collapses now ("clusters of decision records that collapse into one rewritten record each", lines 30-31; 87 keepers → ~14 families) while the decision-record chain is empty: `lint_basis.py --derive-chain decision-record` returns all-empty, status draft (empirically run; only `decision-brief` — a presentation-request type, not the ADR/PDR type, see `basis/artifacts/decision-brief.md:16-25` — has a complete approved chain). What one decision record may carry — its scope, size, one-decision-or-many — is exactly what the run-2 typedef/guideline/fitness will define; the collapse pre-empts it. Violated principle: **`define-good-up-front`** (the activity — collapse-mapping — operates with no stated definition of good), with `governed-context` as the accessory.
Consequence: approving Ask 1 approves record granularity for a type whose definition of good does not exist; when the chain review later defines it, either the approved table is wrong or the chain is retro-fitted to the table — the check would be shaped by the thing it checks.

**F6 — BLOCKER — Run structure contradicts the process's scope rule, and the contradiction is circular.**
Evidence: `definition-chain-migration.md:40-42` — "one run migrates one artifact type." Run 2 bundles adr+pdr while explicitly deferring whether they are one type or two into that same run's review ("the chain review settles the standing kind-set question (ADR vs PDR boundary, RACI)", plan lines 71-74). Run 4 bundles four types (intent, candidate, brief, session; line 78). Run 3 bundles spec chapters, README, current-state, and a `structurizr/` DSL directory (lines 75-77) under a type ("framework spec") with no typedef anywhere in `basis/artifacts/`.
Consequence: the keeper partition (87 / 28 / …) is fixed by a type boundary that the run itself is supposed to decide — if the review splits ADR from PDR (or session from brief), the approved run structure and keeper counts are invalidated mid-run. The run order cannot be approved until the type set is at least provisionally ruled.

**F7 — BLOCKER — Vocabulary: "kind" seven times, against an approved glossary term and a numbered authority ruling.**
Evidence: plan lines 72, 181, 215, 228, 233, 245, 307 vs `basis/glossary.md:21-22` ("**artifact type** — … Not 'kind'") and `basis/README.md` R9 (~lines 243-250): "'kind', coined beside the already-defined 'artifact type', is removed everywhere" — described as `use-defined-terms`' "first conviction."
Consequence: the authority cannot approve, in the first Phase-1 instrument, the exact term whose removal was his first recorded ruling; approval as written re-violates R9. (Trivial to fix; blocking only in the sense that the document is unapprovable as written.)
Extended sweep, same principle: **"keep"** and **"authority-call"** are used as actions (plan lines 26-27; rows 141, 153, 154, 208, 263, 311) but `glossary.md:84-85` closes the action enum at "keep-rewrite, retire, or terminal"; "authority-call" is not even in the plan's own Actions vocabulary (lines 25-29); "keep (regenerate)" (line 315) is a sixth variant. Undefined terms also used: *lane*, *census*, *pins*, *origin-cited*, *provenance spine* (line 348), *trust break* (in-doc gloss only), *RACI* (line 72, bare initialism).

**F8 — MAJOR — The authority's review surface over the mass rewrite is undefined: "the attention architecture" exists nowhere.**
Evidence: `definition-chain-migration.md:236` — "authority spot-checks per the attention architecture" — the phrase's only occurrence in the entire basis and workspace (verified by grep). Trace of actual authority touchpoints per run: (1) `authority-review` (lines 158-167): the chain plus **one** exemplar keeper, verdict clean/tradeoffs/findings, round cap 3; (2) `approve-chain` (lines 202-213): stamps the chain documents; (3) undefined spot-checks during `rewrite-keepers`. So the authority rules **per chain** (once) and **per one exemplar** (once); **per family** — never as such; **per artifact** — only via an undefined sampling clause. For run 2 that means ~87 keepers collapsing into family records with exactly one authority-inspected specimen and no defined sample thereafter.
Consequence: David's question 2(c) has no answer in the material because the material doesn't contain one. This needs an authority-defined attention contract before run 2 at the latest.

**F9 — MAJOR — The plan misstates chain readiness, and states no per-run entry conditions.**
Evidence, empirical (via `lint_basis.py --derive-chain` on the basis checkout): principle-set = typedef only, 1 of 6 links, status draft — the plan's "chain nearly complete" (lines 68-69) is false; decision-record = 0/6; finding = 0/6; session-record = 2/6 (process + role; the plan's "partly exists", line 79, is fair); framework-spec / intent / candidate / brief = no links at all; the only complete approved chain in `basis/` is `decision-brief` — a meta-layer type not in the run order. The plan does say the run builds the chain ("one `definition-chain-migration` run builds a chain and rewrites that type's keepers through it", lines 23-24) — but says it once, in a vocabulary paragraph, and never states per-run entry conditions: no keeper-extraction mechanism (the table is hand-parsed markdown), no statement of which chain links pre-exist per run, no tooling preconditions, no target tree/branch for where chains and rewritten records land (the basis lives on `experiment/new-basis` at a separate checkout; the corpus on `main`; the plan mentions neither branch once).
Consequence: a reader — including the authority — cannot tell from the plan that rewriting is even possible, nor where its outputs go. This is the communication half of the readiness objection.

**F10 — MAJOR — The census arithmetic is wrong in three places, undermining the "four independent lanes, verified" claim.**
Evidence (all verified against disk): Appendix A "drafts/ (18)" (line 352) actually enumerates **19** files (17 loose retires + 2 skills files; disk confirms 18 loose md besides the plan itself, minus 1 keep-rewrite = 17). "findings/archive/ (56)" (line 388) enumerates 9+13+19+14 = **55**, and disk has exactly 55 md files in archive. Run 5 says "the other **95** retire" (line 81) while Appendix headers sum to **96**; the disk answer is 95 (99 findings md − 4 keepers). The lane-D total of 115 only works with the corrected subgroup numbers (19+95+1), i.e., the headers and the total were computed from different counts. Also unit-mixing: 7 terminal *trees* counted as 7 *records* in a table titled "records total (md)" (lines 48-50, 330-331), and the scenarios authority-call cell counts pins (6) in a column that counts records elsewhere.
Consequence: the census was not mechanically derived and was not actually verified; every count in Ask 1 inherits doubt.

**F11 — MAJOR — Opaque references a reader cannot resolve from the document.**
Evidence: `lead-jozud.2` (line 73) — a bd bead id; its meaning ("artifact contract set = set question + kind", the merged kind/RACI investigation) is recoverable only from `sessions/sess-2026-08-05-a.md:9,95` and `pdr-039.md:121`. "the sc06 scenario body in the memory close-out" (line 104) and "sc06-deferral clause" (line 132) — unexplained. "doctrine-loop exit" (line 217), "doctrine-loop record" (line 137) — the Phase-0 loop of sess-2026-08-04-a, unexplained. "the prior census" / "153-hash retirement" (lines 53-54, 342) — uncited. "the authority's 2026-07-04 'no current use' ruling" (line 313) — no citation. "Peters grant" (line 173). "memory-archive pattern" (line 340) — half-glossed. "RETIRED markers" (line 298).
Consequence: Ask 1 requires ruling on rows whose evidence cells point outside the document — the same defect class the F-codes headline.

**F12 — MAJOR — One keeper is covered by no run: `drafts/artifact-system-restructuring.md`.**
Evidence: lane D keep-rewrite list (lines 320-327) includes it ("the initiative this plan executes"); the run order (lines 65-84) covers principle-set, decisions, framework spec, PM records, findings, scenarios — no run rewrites a draft/initiative type.
Consequence: O2's "none silently dropped" is violated by construction before any run starts. Related minor: `drafts/migration-plan.md` itself appears in no lane — the census's self-exclusion is unstated.

**F13 — MAJOR — The plan is itself an artifact of an undefined type, judged by nothing.**
Evidence: frontmatter `type: migration-plan` (line 2); no migration-plan typedef, guideline, or fitness set exists in `basis/artifacts/` or `basis/fitness/` (only `decision-brief.fitness.md` exists). The basis's own guiding statement (`definition-chain-migration.md:21-23`): "A document in an undefined format is source material for a rewrite, never a usable artifact." The process nonetheless depends on it ("The order of runs comes from the approved migration plan", lines 40-42).
Consequence: by the new basis's own law, the instrument that starts Phase 1 is not a usable artifact. Either the authority explicitly rules a bootstrap exception, or the type gets a seed-layer definition first (`define-good-up-front`).

**F14 — MAJOR — The prior cold-read pass was structurally defective.**
Evidence: commit c872505 claims "cold-read repaired … vocabulary + Appendix A added." The only cold-read apparatus in the basis is `roles/cold-reviewer.md` — spec'd for **decision-briefs** (~5 minutes' attention, budgets ≤ ~1,500 words per `artifacts/decision-brief.md`, judged by `fitness/decision-brief.fitness.md`), forbidden to read the annex. The plan is 393 lines with 318 rulable rows. A compliant cold reviewer (a) could never verify F-code referents, because the family map lives outside the document he is forbidden to leave, and per his own role card ("an ask you cannot decide is a defect", "per-ask decidability verdict: … cannot decide") should have returned *cannot decide* on Ask 1; (b) was applied out of type — no migration-plan fitness exists, so "pass" was measured against nothing. Mechanism of the false pass: the rev-2 vocabulary paragraph satisfied the letter of "every term introduced before use" (F-codes get a one-line gloss at lines 29-31) while the *referent* — which records collapse into what — stayed unresolvable; introduction-checking was substituted for decidability-checking. The real reader then failed exactly where the check should have.

**F15 — MAJOR — No running-system demonstration defines "done" (delivery-verified).**
Evidence: the process's derived checks (lines 259-267) are counts and status stamps — artifacts existing and checks passing, which principle `delivery-verified` says "MUST NOT count as done on their own." Neither the plan nor the process names what demonstrates a rewritten corpus working: e.g., compiled skills load and pour, the gate runs green over the new tree, the watcher/primers operate citing rewritten records, `lint_basis` clean over the whole baseline. The plan's own "Edge closure verified" (line 347) is a graph property, not a system demonstration; and the overall migration (as opposed to each run) declares no exit or budget in the plan — the reached-state lives only in `glossary.md:59-61` ("rebaseline"), uncited.

**F16 — MINOR — Archive semantics described three inconsistent ways.**
Plan line 340: "archive branches" (plural), "parentless branch, never on `main`"; process lines 104-106: "in-repo archive branch plus snapshot tag" (singular). One archive contract must be the single source before `archive-move` is built.

**F17 — MINOR — Sequencing hazards inside the keeper set.** `sess-2026-08-04-a` is status **open** yet keep-rewrite (line 288) — rewriting the anchor of a still-open doctrine loop; `pdr-039` "flips accepted at doctrine-loop exit" (line 217) — a run-2 keeper whose status depends on a loop with no scheduled exit.

**F18 — MINOR — No Sources / external form (external-standards-first).** The plan adopts no external migration/register form and records no gap justifying the bespoke five-table structure; every basis typedef carries a Sources section, the Phase-1 instrument carries none.

Consistency checks that **passed** (reported for completeness): lane A rows = 108 on disk (adr 69 + pdr 39; gaps 003/007/044/pdr-008 genuinely absent) with 87/17/4 verified by count; lane B = 67 on disk, 28 keepers verified; lane C pin arithmetic (893 = 860+27+6) internally consistent; all six authority-call rows map onto Ask 2's three rulings and vice versa; `tools/compile_process.py` and `tools/lint_basis.py --derive-chain` exist and run; `bin/gen-scenario-refs` exists for run 6; the `park` step's `bd create` does not breach the memory freeze (which covers `bd remember`/`forget` only).

## Principle screen of the plan (one verdict each)

| Principle | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| define-good-up-front | **FAIL** | F5 (collapse before chain), F13 (plan's own type undefined, checked by an out-of-type fitness — F14) |
| governed-context | **FAIL** | F4 — executing run 2 requires loading the retired rebaseline-bill or an unsanctioned equivalent |
| no-orphan-activities | **FAIL** | F3 (retire/terminal/regenerate/junk-delete belong to no process); overall migration exit uncited in-plan (F15); run 6 is a non-run under a "one run per type" heading |
| use-defined-terms | **FAIL** | F7 — "kind" ×7 against R9; keep/authority-call outside the action enum; lane, census, pins, spine undefined |
| external-standards-first | **MARGINAL FAIL** | F18 — no Sources, no recorded gap |
| single-source-of-truth | **FAIL** | F10 — counts hand-duplicated across summary/run-order/appendix and already divergent (95 vs 96, 55 vs 56, 18 vs 19); F4 — F-map homed in a retired doc; F16 — archive described three ways |
| feedback-loops-with-consumers | **PASS (narrow)** | Ask-2 silence routes to a named consumer (decision-chain review, lines 38-41); park files a bd finding; exemplar friction routes to the authority. Gap: no measurement consumer for the migration itself |
| delivery-verified | **FAIL** | F15 — done = counts + stamps; no running-system demonstration named anywhere |
| least-context | **FAIL** | F4 — the process's input surface cannot carry the plan's operative directives, so they arrive ungoverned or not at all |

## B) REQUIRED CONDITIONS TO PROCEED (before run 1 starts)

1. **Migration-runner tooling present** — **SATISFIED**: `tools/compile_process.py`, `tools/lint_basis.py --derive-chain` (lint_basis.py:26,186,223) exist and execute; `bin/gen-scenario-refs` exists for run 6.
2. **Ask-2 rulings resolvable without blocking** — **SATISFIED**: all three carry recommendations and silence-defaults routing to the decision-chain review (plan lines 88-105); none gates run 1.
3. **Fix the process control flow** (`derive-chain` → `exemplar-rewrite` edge, F2) and recompile — **LEAD-WORK** to patch; the process is status approved, so the amended definition returns to the **AUTHORITY** for re-approval.
4. **Build and approve `archive-move`** (F1) — **LEAD-WORK** to build against a single archive contract; **AUTHORITY-RULING** required because the process names this plan's review as the approving body: *what is the archive contract — one parentless branch or per-run branches, snapshot tag or not?* (F16 folds in here.)
5. **Give the retire/terminal mass a process** (F3) — **LEAD-WORK**: either extend `definition-chain-migration` with an action-table input driving `archive-retired`, or define a separate mechanical close-out process (with declared exit) covering the 163 retires, 14 terminals, and scenario-refs regeneration; authority approves the definition.
6. **Home the F-family map in a governed artifact and give it a channel** (F4) — **LEAD-WORK**: enumerate F1–F15 with membership and target counts inside the plan (or a plan appendix that survives), and add a typed process input (e.g., `$ref: action-table`) so the collapse map and per-keeper directives reach `rewrite-keepers` lawfully.
7. **Rule the collapse question's timing** (F5) — **AUTHORITY-RULING**: *does the approved table fix record granularity now, or does it only nominate families, with granularity decided by the run-2 chain review?* The plan must state whichever answer is given; as written it silently does the former.
8. **Settle the type set for runs 2–4, or amend the process scope note** (F6) — **AUTHORITY-RULING**: *is decision-record one type or two (ADR/PDR), and are intent/candidate/brief/session four chains or one?* — this is lead-jozud.2; deferring it into run 2's own review while run 2's structure presupposes an answer is circular. Minimum viable ruling: a provisional type list for the run order, revisable at each chain review.
9. **Define the attention architecture** (F8) — **AUTHORITY-RULING**: *what does the authority personally inspect during mass rewrite — sampling rate, per-family sign-off, veto window?* — then **LEAD-WORK** to write it into the process or a guideline. Must exist before run 2; run 1 (small) can proceed on chain+exemplar review alone if the authority says so explicitly.
10. **Purge "kind" and reconcile the action vocabulary** (F7) — **LEAD-WORK**: replace all seven uses per R9; either add `keep` and `authority-call` to the glossary's action definition (authority approves the glossary change) or restate those rows in enum terms.
11. **Correct the census arithmetic and regenerate counts mechanically** (F10) — **LEAD-WORK**: drafts 19, archive 55, findings-retire 95 reconciled everywhere; ideally emit the tables from a script so summary/appendix cannot diverge again.
12. **Cover the orphan keeper** (F12) — **LEAD-WORK**: assign `drafts/artifact-system-restructuring.md` to a run (or re-action it), and state the plan's own self-exclusion from the census.
13. **State per-run entry conditions and the target tree** (F9) — **LEAD-WORK**: per run — keeper list source (mechanical extraction), pre-existing chain links (per the lint output, not prose claims — fix "chain nearly complete"), tools required, the branch/checkout where chains and rewritten records land, and how `experiment/new-basis` relates to `main` during Phase 1. The branch-landing question ends in an **AUTHORITY-RULING**: *when does the basis become `main`?*
14. **Resolve or gloss every opaque reference in-document** (F11) — **LEAD-WORK**: lead-jozud.2, sc06, doctrine loop, RACI, prior census citation, 2026-07-04 ruling location, Peters grant, memory-archive pattern.
15. **Name the running-system demonstration for run-done and migration-done** (F15) — **LEAD-WORK** to propose (gate green over new tree, compiled renderings load, lint clean, primers cite rewritten records), **AUTHORITY** accepts it as the done-standard.
16. **Rule the plan's own type standing** (F13) — **AUTHORITY-RULING**: *explicit bootstrap exception for `type: migration-plan`, or a seed-layer typedef first?* Either answer is fine; the silence is not.
17. **Re-run the cold read under a fit-for-purpose check** (F14) — **LEAD-WORK**: after conditions 6, 10-14, a fresh cold reviewer whose brief is per-ask decidability of *this* document type (row-rulability sampling, reference-resolvability), not decision-brief budgets.

## C) Verdict on the readiness objection

David's objection is **partially structurally correct, and the remainder is a communication gap the plan earned**. He is empirically right that the definitions of the migrated types do not exist — the linter returns empty chains for decision-record, finding, and framework-spec, 1/6 for principle-set, 2/6 for session-record, and the only complete approved chain in the basis (`decision-brief`) is a meta-layer type absent from the run order — but the process was designed for exactly that state: `build-chain` authors all six links inside each run, before any rewrite, and the plan does say so in one clause (lines 23-24), so "it would not be possible to rewrite anything" is not literally true *by design*. It is, however, true *as written*, three times over: the approved process's flow physically dead-ends before the exemplar (F2), the archive step blocks on a tool nobody has built or asked to approve (F1/F3), and — the structural core — the plan already makes definition-dependent decisions (the F-family collapses, the scrub/recover directives) that presuppose the very typedefs the runs have yet to create, then homes those decisions in a document it retires and gives them no lawful channel into the process (F4/F5). So the precise mechanism is: the *chains* can be built just-in-time, but the *plan's judgments about what the chains will permit* cannot be — and the document's failure to surface its own build-chain dependency, entry conditions, and tool gaps means the one reader who had to see this could only conclude, correctly in effect if not in mechanism, that nothing can be rewritten yet.
